title: ReSBM: Region-based Scale and Minimal-Level Bootstrapping Management for FHE via Min-Cut
problem: In RNS-CKKS fully homomorphic encryption, repeated homomorphic multiplications escalate ciphertext scale and consume multiplicative levels, requiring expensive bootstrapping to restore capacity; existing compile-time approaches do not efficiently minimize the number and placement of bootstrapping operations, leading to excess overhead in encrypted ML inference.
motivation: FHE-based privacy-preserving ML is bottlenecked by bootstrapping cost, which dominates latency; minimizing bootstrapping insertions at compile time is essential for practical encrypted inference.
method: ReSBM partitions the FHE computation graph into regions using a min-cut graph algorithm that identifies the minimal set of bootstrapping insertion points needed to prevent ciphertext level overflow. Within each region, scale management is handled to keep multiplicative levels within bounds. The min-cut formulation finds a provably minimal-bootstrapping schedule at compile time, reducing the number of costly bootstrapping operations without sacrificing correctness. This is coupled with region-level scale assignment to prevent capacity overflow throughout encrypted inference.
key_novelty: Framing FHE bootstrapping placement as a min-cut problem on the computation graph to find a provably minimal bootstrapping schedule at compile time.
contributions: Region-based scale management that tracks and bounds multiplicative level consumption across computation regions
Min-cut-based algorithm for finding minimal bootstrapping insertion points in FHE computation graphs
Compile-time framework (ReSBM) for rapid encrypted inference with reduced bootstrapping overhead
Demonstrated improvements in FHE-based ML inference latency

metrics.other: reduced number of bootstrapping operations vs prior approaches (not quantified in abstract)

baselines: prior RNS-CKKS scale and bootstrapping management approaches
limitations: Results are limited to compile-time static graphs; dynamic or data-dependent FHE computations may require different approaches.
primary_theme: Min-cut-based bootstrapping minimization for FHE encrypted inference
